title: STILL PRESENT (r2): single-slot refcheck_edit — a second action choice or any action success still discards another row's in-progress typed trio
evidence:
RefcheckSubstitute -> #(
  Model(
    ..menu_closed,
    refcheck_edit: Some(prefill_refcheck_edit(
      model,
      call_id,
      RefcheckEditSubstitute,
    )),
  ),
  effect.none(),
)
...
refcheck_edit: None,
detail: Cancel-now-closes was fixed (UserCancelledRefcheckEdit sets None), but the model is still one Option(RefcheckEdit): opening Correct/Substitute for a second row overwrites the first row's typed values, and any action success clears the other row's open edit — typed referee PII lost.
recommended_fix: In UserChoseRefcheckAction, keep an existing open edit when it targets a different call (or store per-call edits), and clear refcheck_edit on success only when the edit's call_id matches.

title: Wrong-person awaiting transition lacks the taken_over_at UPDATE guard — a concurrent take-over can still yank a landlord-handled row into the correction loop
evidence:
case row.taken_over_at != "" {
  True -> wisp.redirect(to: "/reference/" <> token)
  False ->
    ...
    sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, ...)
--- update_reference_call_status(reference_call_id: UUID, new_status: ...)
WHERE id = $1
  AND status = $5::reference_call_status
detail: The delivery-failure path guards both find and mark (mark_awaiting_correction.sql has taken_over_at IS NULL) and exhaust_reference_call.sql guards too, but this third awaiting writer only checks taken_over_at at read time: a take-over landing between the token read and the UPDATE succeeds (status unchanged by takeover), leaving awaiting_correction + taken_over_at set.
recommended_fix: Scope the wrong-person leg to a guarded transition (add taken_over_at IS NULL to its WHERE — via a dedicated query so update_reference_call_status's other callers are unaffected).
